value.body: A two-year master's degree in economic theory, econometrics and applied fields such as development, public finance, trade and finance. An M.Sc / quantitative economics variant puts more weight on mathematics and statistics. It is the standard route into economic research, policy work, teaching and the Indian Economic Service.

items.label: PG students in Economics
items.note: Based on institutions that reported data

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, usually in economics; many programmes also want mathematics at Class 12 or UG level. Central universities — including the Delhi School of Economics and JNU — admit through CUET-PG; some institutes such as ISI (M.S. in Quantitative Economics) run their own tests. Check each programme's brochure for subject requirements.

value.title: At a glance
items: Programmes differ a lot in how mathematical they are; quantitative ones expect calculus, linear algebra and statistics.
Common next steps: research assistant or analyst roles, policy and think-tank work, UPSC IES, UGC-NET for teaching, or a Ph.D.
Data and coding skills (R, Python, Stata) widen options in industry.
